root_cause.text: In `drivers/usb/gadget/udc/dummy_hcd.c`, the dummy-hcd emulation of `synchronize_irq()` was executed in `dummy_pullup()` before emulated interrupts were actually disabled in `dummy_udc_async_callbacks()`, creating a race where callbacks could still run after the “synchronization” had completed and before gadget unbind.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `while (dum->callback_usage > 0)` synchronize-emulation loop from `dummy_pullup()` and adds the same loop to `dummy_udc_async_callbacks()` specifically under `if (!enable)`, with the comment that it “has to happen after emulated interrupts are disabled (`dum->ints_enabled` is clear) and before the unbind callback.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the callback-wait loop from dummy pullup handling so the gadget disconnect path no longer blocks in this function.
intent_record.what: The `if (value == 0)` block inside `dummy_pullup()` was removed. That deleted the loop which repeatedly unlocked, slept with `usleep_range(1000, 2000)`, and relocked while `dum->callback_usage > 0` to wait for callback completion.
intent_record.how: After this change, pulling the gadget down no longer waits in `dummy_pullup()` for in-flight callbacks to finish. The function now updates `dum->pullup`, sets the link state, releases the lock, and immediately polls root hub status, which removes the built-in synchronization delay previously used to emulate `synchronize_irq()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wait for outstanding dummy UDC callbacks to finish when disabling async callbacks, matching synchronize_irq-style teardown ordering.
intent_record.what: The function `dummy_udc_async_callbacks()` was modified to add a conditional block executed when `enable` is false. After setting `dum->ints_enabled = enable`, it now waits in a loop while `dum->callback_usage > 0`, temporarily releasing and reacquiring `dum->lock` and sleeping with `usleep_range(1000, 2000)` between checks. A comment explains that this emulates `synchronize_irq()` and must run after interrupts are disabled and before the unbind callback.
intent_record.how: When asynchronous callbacks are being disabled, the code now blocks until any in-flight callback activity has finished instead of returning immediately. This prevents the unbind path from proceeding while callbacks are still executing, reducing the risk of races between interrupt-style callback handling and driver teardown.
